methods.notes: Name only, matched exactly so "MousrDfu" (bootloader) does not match. The Nordic UART service is deliberately not listed here: within a ble_scan method a name and a service are alternatives, and the service alone would match every Nordic UART product. After connecting, confirm 6e400001-b5a3-f393-e0a9-e50e24dcca9e is present before writing anything. A renamed toy is not found by this method; the user picks it from a generic scan and adds it by hand.

identification.notes: Name and service are a narrowing pair: treat an advertisement as this toy only when the name is exactly "Mousr" AND the Nordic UART service is present (advertised, or found on connect before any write). The Nordic UART service on its own identifies nothing; many unrelated products in this catalogue carry it, and this spec declares movement commands. The name is an exact match, not a prefix, so the bootloader name "MousrDfu" is excluded here; it is declared in features[firmware_update].dfu.dfu_mode, which a consumer checks first. The factory name is reported, not observed, and the app lets an owner rename the toy. A renamed unit is not auto-matched: the user adds it by hand.

device.name: Petronics Mousr
device.notes: Phone-direct robotic cat toy. Ordinary operation does not require an account or cloud service. Nordic UART is the command path. The app also references the Nordic Secure DFU service (0000fe59-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb) and its bootloader characteristics; see features. An earlier note misread the 8ec9000x DFU characteristics as a Laird virtual serial port; no Laird VSP UUID (569a1101-…) was recorded for this toy. The app bundles recovery firmware, but no update was performed and no firmware is shipped in this spec. Movement and tail calibration require a clear area and supervision.

openness.notes: No public protocol implementation was found. Wire facts are derived from the recovered official app's packet builders and command metadata, not from a live capture.

enter_pairing_mode.indicator: LED blinks blue every 4 seconds while waiting for a Bluetooth connection (sleep mode).
enter_pairing_mode.notes: No pairing mode, but a power state matters: in power down (after a 2-second pushbutton hold, or when charging completes) Bluetooth is off and the toy does not advertise. Click the chin pushbutton to wake it; in sleep mode it advertises without a press. The guide's "pairing" is the app's device list, not an OS Bluetooth step.

exclusivity.notes: The user guide expects one toy to be driven from several phones in turn (each phone keeps its own name for the toy), which rules out a one-owner binding. Whether a second central can connect while one is already connected is not established.
exclusivity.recovery: Close the Mousr app on every other phone or tablet before connecting; the app connects on its own when it finds only one toy, so an open app elsewhere can take it first. If it still does not appear, wake it with the chin pushbutton (it is invisible in power down), and as a last resort hold the pushbutton 15 seconds for device recovery mode, then click once to reboot.

pairing.notes: The user guide (v1.1, 2018) describes connecting as: press the chin pushbutton, open the app, tap the toy in the app's device list. No PIN, no confirmation on the toy and no step in the phone's Bluetooth settings appear, and it notes that a toy driven from several phones is named separately on each — so the name lives app-side and the toy keeps no per-phone record. Static analysis of the app likewise found no application-layer authentication for normal commands. That makes "connect and go" the reading every source supports, but none has been replayed: confidence stays low until someone connects from a host that never ran the app, and `bonding` stays unknown because an OS that pairs on an insufficient-authentication error would hide a demand for one. The device recovery mode (15-second hold) clears the toy's internal memory; it is a reboot, not an unpairing, and there is nothing to unpair.

safety_advisory.detail: Test the stop command first and use movement only in a clear area away from pets, people, cables and edges. The app-derived drive values have no proven physical units. Do not attempt DFU until normal control and charging state are established.
safety_advisory.summary: Moving robot and tail assembly — supervise use.

credentials.notes: No account-bound credential was found for ordinary operation.

factory_reset.description: No general factory-reset procedure is established. DFU and tail calibration are not resets.
factory_reset.effect: Not established: whether autonomous-play settings, calibration or pairing state are cleared is undocumented. DFU and tail calibration are not factory resets.

methods.description: Connect over Nordic UART, enable notifications, then send documented 15-byte commands.
methods.name: Connect and subscribe

steps.action: Charge and wake the toy in a clear area.
Connect to the Nordic UART service and enable notifications on 6e400003-b5a3-f393-e0a9-e50e24dcca9e.
Send the stop command before testing any other command, and check that it is accepted (see the code-byte note on the command input characteristic).

setup.notes: No account or first-run cloud activation was found in the recovered app. Connect directly and subscribe before sending commands; this has not been replayed on a toy.

rejoin.notes: BLE-only; reconnect after the previous central disconnects.

testing.notes: Not driven against hardware by this project. The 15-byte envelope, command codes and float32 drive-vector layout come from static analysis of the recovered official 1.0.7 app. The second code byte of a one-digit command code is unresolved (see the command input notes). Notification payload layouts, auto-mode offsets and drive-value physical scaling remain unverified.

artifacts.artifact: Recovered official Mousr app 1.0.7, packet builders and command metadata, read 2026-11-01
artifacts.description: Establishes the 15-byte command envelope, decimal command codes, float32-LE drive vector, Nordic UART and notification vocabulary. These are reported facts from static analysis, not hardware tests.

artifacts.artifact: Mousr User Guide v1.2 recovered from that app
artifacts.description: Supports phone-direct operation and supplies movement/tail calibration precautions. No firmware compatibility claim is made.

evidence.open_questions: Drive-value ranges and physical units, notification payload layouts, auto-mode configuration offsets, bonding requirements, firmware/DFU compatibility, the second code byte of one-digit command codes, and whether the factory name is exactly "Mousr".

dfu_mode.notes: Bootloader name recorded from the app, not observed on a unit. Address behaviour is not observed; a stock nRF5 SDK bootloader without bond sharing would advertise at address+1. A device in this mode gets no ordinary controls.

enter.notes: The command vocabulary has a bootloader-entry code (8), but its payload and code-byte form are not established, so it is not declared as a command. Whether the running application also exposes the stack's buttonless characteristic (8ec90003-f315-4f60-9fb8-838830daea50) is not established.

image.format: nrfutil DFU zips: three application packages and one SoftDevice/bootloader package bundled in the app.
image.notes: The images stay in the app; none is shipped here. Whether this bootloader enforces the stack's default ECDSA signature check is not established.

dfu.notes: From the app's Nordic DFU library references and bundled packages, not from an update performed on hardware. Do not attempt an update until ordinary control and charging state are established.

recovery.notes: The nRF5 SDK defaults (dual-bank where flash allows, 120 s inactivity timeout back to a valid application) have not been checked on a toy.

helpful_urls.title: Mousr Kickstarter FAQ

initialization.notes: Enable the UART notification channel before control.

CommandPacket.description: The fixed 15-byte Nordic UART command envelope.

fields.description: Offsets 13-14. A two-digit code is two ASCII digits. A one-digit code is unresolved between form A (ASCII 0 then the digit) and form B (the digit then NUL); see the command input notes.
fields.name: decimal_code

parse_rules: Reject packets whose total length is not exactly 15 bytes.
The move command places three little-endian IEEE-754 binary32 values at offsets 1, 5 and 9, then code 2 (form A 30 32 as declared; form B would be 32 00).
Do not label the drive values as physical speed, degrees or percent without new evidence.

NotificationVocabulary.description: Recovered notification IDs, not complete payload declarations.

one_digit_code_forms.note: Both candidate encodings of every one-digit code, as the last two bytes of the 15-byte packet. Neither is backed by an observation.

protocol_details.undeclared_controls: Auto-mode byte offsets, debug-log transfer, tail calibration, driver assist, tutorial control, set time and bootloader entry (code 8) are not declared as commands because their payload, or the code-byte form, is not established. They are listed above so the next person can capture them, not withheld. No reset or firmware write should be inferred from the command number alone.

remaining_unknowns: Drive values are app control values, not established m/s, degrees or percent.
Notification IDs are known but payload layouts are not; no battery or pose decoder is declared.
Auto-mode configuration has a 12-byte payload but its exact offsets are unresolved.
The app carries Nordic DFU packages, but no update sequence or version compatibility was tested.

One-digit command codes (stop 0, spin 1, move 2, reset heading 3, turn off 9) have two contradictory encodings in the analysis: ASCII 0 then the digit, or the digit then NUL. Neither was observed; the declared values mix them. A capture of the app sending stop and move settles it.
The factory advertised name is reported as exactly Mousr but has not been seen on a unit; identification uses it as an exact name.
No hardware capture confirms bonding, command acceptance or connection limits.

move.advanced_reason: Drives a moving robot. Use only small values in a clear area after testing the stop command; physical scaling is not established.
move.description: Send a raw drive vector (command 2); units and valid ranges are unverified. Declared in form A (code bytes 30 32); form B would end 32 00.

angle.description: Raw app control value, not proven degrees.

hold.description: Raw app control value; valid range is unestablished.

speed.description: Raw app control value, not proven m/s, percent or another physical unit.

reset_heading.description: Reset the toy's heading reference used by autonomous movement (command 3). Declared in form A (code bytes 30 33); form B would end 33 00.

sleep.description: Enter sleep mode until the toy is woken (command 10).

spin.advanced_reason: Starts movement; use in a clear area after testing the stop command.
spin.description: Start the spin action (command 1). Declared in form A (code bytes 30 31); form B would end 31 00.

stop.description: Stop movement (command 0). Declared in form B (code bytes 30 00); form A would end 30 30.

turn_off.description: Power the toy off, ending the session (command 9). Declared in form A (code bytes 30 39); form B would end 39 00.

characteristics.name: Command input
characteristics.notes: Every declared command is exactly 15 bytes: ASCII 30, a 12-byte payload (zero-filled when unused), then the command code in offsets 13-14. A two-digit code is its two ASCII digits (18 is 31 38). For a one-digit code the second byte is UNRESOLVED: the static analysis this spec rests on yielded two contradictory readings and no capture settles it. Form A is a leading ASCII zero then the digit (code 2 is 30 32); form B is the digit then NUL (code 2 is 32 00). The declared values below keep the bytes the analysis recorded for each command, which mix the two forms (stop is form B, the others form A), so every one-digit command is marked verification hypothesis and its description gives the other form. A client should try stop in both forms and keep whichever the toy obeys.

characteristics.name: UART notifications
characteristics.notes: Notification IDs are recovered, but their complete payload layouts are not. Keep the value opaque until a capture confirms the envelope rather than presenting guessed battery or pose readings.

characteristics.name: DFU control point (bootloader)
characteristics.notes: Nordic Secure DFU control point, present in the bootloader. Properties on this unit are not observed; do not write outside a deliberate update.

characteristics.name: DFU packet (bootloader)
characteristics.notes: Nordic Secure DFU packet characteristic, present in the bootloader. Properties on this unit are not observed; do not write outside a deliberate update.

services.name: Nordic Secure DFU service
services.notes: Firmware-update path, recorded from the app's UUID references, not from a GATT dump of a toy. 8ec90001-f315-4f60-9fb8-838830daea50 (DFU control point) and 8ec90002-f315-4f60-9fb8-838830daea50 (DFU packet) are the stack's bootloader characteristics; they were previously mislabelled here as a Laird VSP service. Whether the running application exposes the stack's buttonless characteristic is not established. A GATT explorer lists this service read-only; see features.
